import pandas as pd

# Data lives in its own data/ subfolder, separate from code -- a habit
# worth keeping as this repo grows. Use forward slashes in the path,
# even on Windows: Python/pandas accept them on every OS, so the same
# code runs unchanged whether you're on Windows, Mac, or Linux. A
# single backslash (data\file.csv) is NOT safe here -- Python reads
# backslashes as escape characters inside a string, which can silently
# produce the wrong path.
df = pd.read_csv("data/macro_var_synthetic.csv", parse_dates=["date"])
dict(value=len(df))
```

#| content: valuebox

```

## Row {height=80%}

```{python}
#| title: "Output Gap, Inflation, and Policy Rate"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (11, 4)

tab10 = plt.get_cmap("tab10")
colors = {"output_gap": tab10(0), "inflation": tab10(1), "policy_rate": tab10(2)}

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for var in variables:
    ax.plot(df["date"], df[var], label=var, color=colors[var], linewidth=1.2)
ax.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=False)
ax.set_xlim(df["date"].min(), df["date"].max())
plt.show()
```
